evaluation.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0002","evidenceText":"Since the BLE does account for reservoir inundation, some of the BLE reservoir inundation extents extend beyond the NWM reservoir geometries contributing to false negatives (FNs), or under-prediction.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0003","evidenceText":"To calculate these secondary metrics, one and false negatives (FN), or type II errors, which is wet in the benchmark but predicted dry.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0005","evidenceText":"Lastly, the reader may come across true negatives (TN) which is defined as dry in both","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0006","evidenceText":"the benchmark and predicted datasets.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0007","evidenceText":"In other words, POD is an indicator of model skill in inundated regions while FAR is an indicator of model skill in non-inundated regions.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0008","evidenceText":"This data set was selected due to its large spatial coverage, availability of cross-sections with streamflow information, higher level of sophistication when compared to HAND, engineering scale detail, and a storied use in the literature as an evaluation data set (Afshari et al., [2018](#page-27-11); Bates et al., [2016;](#page-27-28) Cook & Merwade, [2009;](#page-27-29) Criss & Nelson, [2022;](#page-27-30) Follum et al., [2017](#page-28-30); Hu & Demir, [2021](#page-28-31); Li & Demir, [2022](#page-28-32); Li et al., [2022;](#page-28-33) Rajib et al., [2016;](#page-29-33) Wing et al., [2017;](#page-30-31) Wing et al., [2017](#page-30-31); Zheng, Maidment, et al., [2018](#page-30-12); Zheng, Maidment, et al., [2018](#page-30-12)).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0009","evidenceText":"Some work by Gerapetritis and Pelissier ([2004\\)](#page-28-34) denotes CSI a good proxy for measuring a forecasting system's utility in protecting life and property and has been shown as mathematically optimized when POD = 1 − FAR.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0010","evidenceText":"While these metrics are commonly employed in the evaluation of FIM and binary weather prediction communities in general, they do come with some notable limitations including frequency dependence in the case of CSI and FAR (Gerapetritis & Pelissier, [2004](#page-28-34); Jolliffe & Stephenson, [2012](#page-28-35); Schaefer, [1990;](#page-29-34) Stephens et al., [2014](#page-30-32)).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0011","evidenceText":"Using the NWM as a source of streamflow input would be a logical choice due to its operational use, but this would introduce hydro-climatic uncertainties that could impact the results of adding a multi-fluvial source extension to HAND.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0012","evidenceText":"On the other hand, relying on point sources of streamflow or stage, such as gages, would eliminate this limitation, but limit the information available to only a single source of inundation at a specific site.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0013","evidenceText":"Figure [8](#page-16-1) illustrates both NWM V2.1 and BLE flowpaths as well as the BLE cross-sections that have recurrence discharges associated with them.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0014","evidenceText":"This partially handles the influence of neighboring cross sections that could cause flow discontinuities and mass conservation issues.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0015","evidenceText":"Additionally, the stream network of the InFRM furnished models are of higher stream densities and bifurcation ratios, as evident in Figure [8](#page-16-1), leading to a significant amount of FNs along headwater streams with unit Horton-Strahler order due to the lack of representation of these additional headwater streams in the NWM network.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0016","evidenceText":"The metrics employed in this study to evaluate inundation extents include CSI, Probability of Detection (POD), and False Alarm Ratio (FAR) and are presented in Equations [6](#page-17-0)[–8,](#page-17-1) respectively.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0017","evidenceText":"Thus, frequency dependent statistics should be used with caution when comparing across sites with varying frequencies.","locatorAnchor":null}]}
